detailed_description:
Semi-realistic cinematic 3D CG Chinese animation with crisp high-shutter action clarity, strong physical weight, stable referenced identities, and controlled motion trails in 16:9. The 12.00-second sequence uses exactly four shots and three action-matched cuts at 00:02.500, 00:05.800, and 00:09.600, with no cutaway, hidden contact, time jump, slow motion, replay, action reset, or fresh windup. The cameras never cross to the opposite side of the established action axis; Shot 2 moves onto the protagonist's exact rear extension while Shots 1, 3, and 4 preserve the original side orientation. Every shot keeps both complete bodies, the entire 2.4-meter <Subject 2>, and <Subject 3>'s full airborne trajectory readable. On a vast open grassland at sunset, a low sun from the left casts consistent warm orange-gold rim light, long soft-edged shadows, and warm highlights across metal and moving grass beneath a clear sky. <Subject 1> always uses a correct long-spear grip: his right hand remains immediately beside the butt cap at his right waist, his left hand controls the shaft about forty percent forward from the butt, roughly sixty percent of the shaft projects beyond the left hand toward the enemy, and both hands stay far behind the spearhead.

[Shot 1] A 32mm low-side medium-wide full-body tracking view opens with <Subject 1> on the left and <Subject 3> approaching airborne at his chest height from the right. The camera tracks parallel with small amplitude and a restrained upward tilt, keeping both full silhouettes and the entire spear visible against the sunset grassland. <Subject 1> steps diagonally outside the flight line, sinks his hips, drives from the rear leg, and performs the first and only opening straight thrust, rising into the underside of the enemy's silver upper-chest armor. The chest snaps upward, spine arches, legs lag below, and forward momentum redirects into a clear upward float. The spear shaft flexes; the protagonist's elbows and shoulders recoil briefly before he withdraws along the same line.

From 00:01.400 to 00:02.500, he retracts the thrust and draws the butt beside his right waist. His right foot crosses behind the left and lands on the ball of the foot; both knees remain flexed. Weight transfers onto the crossed right foot, then both forefeet pivot while the left heel releases. Pelvis, waist, rib cage, chest, shoulders, arms, and head follow the same backward turning direction in sequence. His back becomes visible to the enemy for an instant and his head turns last before his eyes reacquire the target. His complete body, including both feet and the whole torso, performs exactly one unmistakable backward 360-degree turn; this is not an upper-body twist and the feet do not stay frozen.

That single body turn directly powers revolution 1 of an authentic continuous traditional Chinese vertical spear flower. Both arms carry <Subject 2> behind his back without touching his body. From one low reference point, spearhead and butt chase each other upward outside his right shoulder in one shared near-vertical circular plane. The reinforced forward shaft immediately behind the spearhead strikes <Subject 3>'s right hip once on the rising quadrant, tipping the pelvis upward. The weapon then passes down in front and returns to the same low reference point exactly as the protagonist's feet and chest finish turning toward the enemy. His crossed foot uncrosses into a stable forward fighting stance, but the spear never stops. Wrists roll continuously, palms alternate pressure, elbows fold and extend, and the shaft rolls through both palms without hand release, grip collapse, reversal, pause, reset, or fresh windup. This is one continuous vertical spear-flower technique, not overhead swings, separate staff strikes, or a generic weapon spin.

[Shot 2] At 00:02.500, cut exactly as revolution 1 completes at the low reference point to a 28mm elevated rear-following wide view positioned directly behind <Subject 1> and slightly above the crown of his head, looking forward over him toward <Subject 3>. The camera tracks forward at the protagonist's advance speed with a stable horizon and no orbit, lateral drift, or axis crossing. Keep the protagonist's complete body in the lower center foreground, the full spearhead-to-butt path clear around rather than hidden by his silhouette, and the enemy fully visible ahead in the upper center. This over-the-head rear angle emphasizes the depth, forward pursuit, and continuous rising contacts while preserving the near-vertical spear-flower plane. The weapon continues through the cut with no pause. <Subject 1> immediately performs revolutions 2 through 6. He does not keep spinning his body after the single backward turn; he faces the enemy and advances with compact shuffle steps while coordinated wrists, forearms, elbows, shoulders, and waist maintain the same circular plane outside and in front of his right shoulder. Every complete revolution strikes exactly once on its rising quadrant with the reinforced forward shaft behind the spearhead, delivering a blunt lifting blow rather than point penetration. Revolutions 2-4 strike the fabric-covered lower ribs, opposite ribs, and lower edge of the silver upper-chest armor. Revolutions 5 and 6 begin four closely spaced contacts across the fabric-covered hips, abdomen, and ribs. At each contact, the shaft visibly bows, the hands and shoulder give a short recoil, the struck region deforms first, and angular momentum carries the spear through the upper arc and back to the same low reference point. End Shot 2 precisely as revolution 6 completes there, with the enemy beginning another gravity-driven drop and the spear already flowing into revolution 7.

[Shot 3] At 00:05.800, match cut on the low reference point to a 50mm strict-profile full-body view with mild telephoto compression. The camera tracks rapidly and parallel to the action with a subtle push-in that never crops either body, the spearhead, or the butt cap. Revolution 7 begins from exactly the prior weapon position and speed. Revolutions 7 and 8 complete the same closely spaced hip, abdomen, and rib contact cluster, stopping each brief descent and rocking <Subject 3> left, right, then center while lifting him. Revolutions 9-12 accelerate to maximum speed: the ninth catches the underside of the pelvis, the tenth and eleventh catch the lower chest from alternating sides, and the twelfth drives through the chest-abdomen line with the strongest blunt lift. The twelve contacts across Shots 1-3 remain one accelerating flower, not isolated attacks. Metal areas dent and vibrate; fabric-covered areas compress and fold without invented plate armor or metal fragments. After every contact, the torso buckles around the blow, limbs and robe whip behind by inertia, the body rotates slightly, upward speed surges, then gravity decelerates it into a slight drop before the next rising arc catches it. The enemy never hovers or moves without force. The continuous spearhead-and-butt wheel stays readable through the angle change, with all twelve contacts visibly distinct. End Shot 3 exactly when revolution 12 returns to the same low reference point and the enemy begins descending into the final thrust line.

[Shot 4] At 00:09.600, match cut to a 24mm low side-front wide view from the same side of the action axis. The camera dollies backward quickly along the launch direction, preserving both full bodies and the entire spear while emphasizing the final kinetic chain. Without stopping, <Subject 1> compresses the circular momentum into a straight line, slides back into the original wide spear grip, lunges beneath the descending <Subject 3>, anchors his left foot, and drives hip, waist, shoulder, and right hand forward in sequence. He performs the second and final straight thrust, rising hard into the center underside of the silver upper-chest armor. The armor caves inward, the upper body snaps back, both legs sling upward a fraction later, and the enemy launches high and far in a backward tumble. From 00:11.400, the dolly decelerates into a restrained pull-back and upward tilt without losing the protagonist. He absorbs recoil through bent knees and elbows, retracts the butt to his right waist, and settles into a low forward-reaching guard while the enemy continues climbing through the orange-gold sunset sky. End at 00:12.000 with both subjects still in motion: the enemy rising and tumbling, grass and robe moving in the evening wind, and the protagonist's spear settling under residual vibration. Preserve coherent anatomy, stable faces and clothing, constant spear length, correct hand placement far behind the spearhead, continuous weapon trajectory, clear contact, and physically credible reactions. No warhammer, saber, firearm, second weapon, weapon transformation, full-body plate armor, body penetration, hand release, random axis crossing, teleportation, unexplained hovering, subtitles, text, logo, or watermark.

overall_soundscape:
Open-grassland evening wind and grass rustle continue without interruption across all three picture cuts. The opening thrust produces one hard shaft whoosh, one deep armor-and-body impact, a brief shaft creak, armor vibration, cloth snap, the protagonist's restrained exertion, and the enemy's expelled breath. The uninterrupted vertical spear flower produces one continuous accelerating circular whistle with no audible reset at either mid-flower cut, punctuated by exactly twelve distinct and increasingly forceful impact beats. Contacts on silver armor use a sharp metallic dent and short armor rattle; contacts on fabric-covered hips, abdomen, ribs, or upper back use dense body thumps and cloth compression without invented metal sounds. Every hit includes a shaft-flex creak, body jolt, robe snap, and immediate return to the same revolving whistle. Compact foot shuffles track the protagonist's advance. The final rising thrust lands with one heavier bass-rich armor-and-body crash, flexing shaft strain, a displaced-air boom, an involuntary pain cry, and fading airborne armor and fabric rattle. No dialogue.
